now: Ladder done (jepa 1422, jepa-h1 1491 Elo). Next: training signal that compares moves (self-play with exploration, search labels).
goal: A bot that decides by imagining futures in a learned latent space (JEPA world model), not by reconstructing boards.

mentalModel.summary: An encoder maps the board to a 96-number latent z. A predictor imagines the latent of my next decision (and 4 decisions on) for each legal move. A value head scores the imagined latents; the best-scoring move is played. Nothing is decoded back to a board.

thoughts.text: JEPA, not a generative world model: the predictor only has to land near the embedding of the future, so it can ignore details it cannot predict (the opponent's hidden hand, draws).

Smoke test on 196 random games: the predicted next latent is the nearest of 512 candidates 70% of the time, against 6% for 'nothing changes'. Linear probes read base HP, hand size and board power back out of z with R² of 0.9 to 0.98.
Two-stage training (JEPA first, value after) stops the value head memorising games: held-out value accuracy went 0.70 to 0.72, and 0.74 with rust-greedy2 games added.
But those versions play worse. Predicting the winner is not the same as ranking moves: an outcome label says who is ahead, not which move was better.

Ladder: jepa-h1 1491, jepa 1422, jepa-pure 1276 Elo. Beats random 9-1, loses to rush 2-8 and rust-greedy2 0-10. Earlier 'beats rush' runs were wrong: eval.js reused rush across games and its loop guard leaked.
